findings.title: From lesson to denial
findings.claim: The opening negation turns from the lesson in the stories to a denial that the discourse belongs to the fabricated-report category.
findings.mechanism: Ma is the carrier; the preceding lesson clause and following hadith-yuftara phrase trigger the shift, so denial introduces the discourse's status.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from what stories teach to what kind of report this is.
findings.containment: The denial does not cancel the lesson in the stories or establish a wider formula.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: A category is denied
findings.claim: Ma rejects a classification before the verse supplies the discourse's positive functions.
findings.mechanism: The negation scopes over the report-and-fabrication clause; the following lakin turns that rejection toward a corrective list.
findings.reader_payoff: The positive account arrives as an answer to a rejected category.
findings.containment: This is local syntax, not a denial that any report can be fabricated.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Presence answered by denial
findings.claim: The repeated copular frame first affirms lesson-bearing presence, then denies fabricated identity.
findings.mechanism: The first kana with fi qasasihim supplies presence and location; the second kana under ma and yuftara supplies the contrasting classification.
findings.reader_payoff: The two clauses answer one another instead of reading as unrelated statements.
findings.containment: The balance is local to these clauses; it does not decide broader claims about narrative.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Categorical non-identity
findings.claim: The negated kana excludes fabricated discourse as a category, not merely as a one-time past event.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the second kana; ma and the passive imperfect yuftara make the predicate a general classification.
findings.reader_payoff: The denial reads as a statement about the discourse's kind.
findings.containment: No agent or account of fabrication is specified.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Report named as the denied class
findings.claim: Hadithan names an indefinite report or discourse category, which the following passive clause denies as fabricated.
findings.mechanism: Hadithan is the carrier; yuftara supplies the rejected production mode, while ma-kana scopes the denial.
findings.reader_payoff: The denial reaches the report category itself, not just one named utterance.
findings.containment: The indefinite noun remains a report category; it does not imply that every report is fabricated.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Fabrication denied as a class
findings.claim: The passive imperfect yuftara denies fabrication as an ongoing category attached to this discourse.
findings.mechanism: The verb is the carrier; hadithan supplies the report being classified and ma-kana scopes the denial.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears more than a claim that no one fabricated this once.
findings.containment: The passive leaves an agent unnamed and does not assert a theory of textual origins.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Fabrication as a tear
findings.claim: The denied fabrication can carry a bounded root image of splitting, set against the neighboring confirmation term.
findings.mechanism: Yuftara carries the damaging-cut branch; tasdiq is an independent focus trigger whose truth-confirming function makes the cut feel like disruption of truth.
findings.reader_payoff: The denial gains a concrete fracture image while fabrication remains the ordinary sense.
findings.containment: The cutting branch is a root resonance, not a lexical replacement or claim about physical composition.

epistemic.reason: The focus forms are supplied and the root branch is registered; the cross-root metaphor remains qualified.

branch_activations.carrier: Yuftara ordinarily names fabrication or false production.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Tasdiq names confirmation in the next corrective list.
branch_activations.activation: The damaging split contacts the separate truth-confirming word, so the denied act can be pictured as a tear against truth.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Fabrication is legible as a fracture set against confirmation, while its local verb sense remains fabrication.
branch_activations.boundary: The image is a root-level resonance, not a morphological gloss of Form VIII.

findings.title: Link into correction
findings.claim: The conjunction keeps the denial connected to the corrective turn introduced by lakin.
findings.mechanism: Wa is the carrier; lakin is the independent trigger that makes the next phrase a continuation and correction.
findings.reader_payoff: The positive account answers the denial rather than beginning as a detached sentence.
findings.containment: The relation is local syntax, not a claim that the list exhausts every function.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Correction remains attached
findings.claim: The positive characterization remains syntactically attached to the denial it corrects.
findings.mechanism: Wa links forward into lakin; the preceding negative clause is the distinct point that lakin rectifies.
findings.reader_payoff: The correction retains the rejected category in view as contrast for what follows.
findings.containment: The conjunction does not erase the denial or collapse the following functions into one.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Brief rejection, fuller account
findings.claim: A short denial of fabrication opens into a longer account of four positive functions.
findings.mechanism: The compact ma-kana-yuftara clause is followed by lakin and the coordinated tasdiq, tafsil, huda, and rahma predicates.
findings.reader_payoff: The imbalance gives the affirmative account more space than the rejected label.
findings.containment: The contrast concerns this verse's structure, not relative rank.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Lakin rectifies the category
findings.claim: Lakin corrects the false classification by introducing the discourse's proper characterization.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is lakin; the preceding negation supplies what is corrected and the four predicates supply the replacement account.
findings.reader_payoff: The turn reads as rectification, not a loose addition after denial.
findings.containment: The correction adds positive functions without displacing the denial.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: A proper substitute follows
findings.claim: The istidrak force of lakin substitutes the positive account for the rejected category.
findings.mechanism: The negative predicate is its trigger; lakin contacts that denial and opens the coordinated functions that follow.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices why the affirmative list follows the brief rejection.
findings.containment: The substitute is the list stated here, not an exhaustive definition of revelation.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Confirmation as an act
findings.claim: Tasdiq presents confirmation as something the discourse does, not only a quality it claims for itself.
findings.mechanism: The accusative verbal noun begins the corrective predicate list and points to alladhi bayna yadayhi as its object.
findings.reader_payoff: Truthfulness becomes a relation to what precedes, not self-assertion alone.
findings.containment: The supplied nominative variant remains possible; this describes the local accusative reading.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Identification arrives through the phrase
findings.claim: The relative pronoun makes the confirmed object definite but lets its relation complete the identification.
findings.mechanism: Alladhi is the carrier; the following bayna-yadayhi phrase supplies the identifying relation.
findings.reader_payoff: Continuity is built by syntax rather than a named title.
findings.containment: The object is identified relationally; no extra antecedent is imposed.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: A definite relation to what precedes
findings.claim: The relative pronoun treats the confirmed object as known through its relation to the present discourse.
findings.mechanism: Alladhi supplies definiteness; the following phrase specifies the relation that makes the object recognizable.
findings.reader_payoff: Continuity is carried by a relative phrase.
findings.containment: The phrase identifies by relation and does not name a specific book or title.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: The spatial phrase marks what precedes
findings.claim: Bayna-yadayhi uses a front or between image as the idiom for what stands before the confirming discourse.
findings.mechanism: Bayna carries the relation; tasdiq and the relative phrase trigger the temporal-scriptural reading within the same clause.
findings.reader_payoff: The spatial wording makes prior material feel present to confirmation.
findings.containment: The idiom's temporal use remains primary; no literal hands are asserted.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: A front-facing relation remains visible
findings.claim: The phrase can be felt first as direct engagement with what stands in front, then as the conventional marker for what precedes.
findings.mechanism: Bayna and yadayhi form the spatial carrier; tasdiq independently makes the relation one of engagement with prior material.
findings.reader_payoff: The confirmation feels directed toward something placed before it.
findings.containment: This is a local image within an established idiom, not a literal scene.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: The dual form compresses the image
findings.claim: Yadayhi preserves a two-hand image inside the conventional phrase meaning what is before it.
findings.mechanism: The dual noun and attached pronoun are the carrier; bayna supplies the relation that conventionalizes the image.
findings.reader_payoff: The idiom retains a bodily shape as it marks precedence.
findings.containment: The phrase functions idiomatically; no physical scene is claimed.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: The body image persists inside the idiom
findings.claim: The before-it phrase can keep the bodily image of two hands audible beneath its temporal use.
findings.mechanism: Yadayhi carries the hand image; bayna independently turns it into a front-facing relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The conventional meaning remains spatially imaginable.
findings.containment: The image does not override the idiom or depend on another verse.

epistemic.reason: The dual hand form and idiomatic relation are focus-local; the bodily image is a qualified resonance.

findings.title: The statement opens emphatically
findings.claim: La-qad frames the focus statement as an emphatic conclusion rather than a neutral next event.
findings.mechanism: The opening lam and qad carry emphasis; the following existential kana is the assertion they frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The lesson claim arrives as a declared judgment on the story material.
findings.containment: The effect is local to this opening, not a surah-level thesis.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: A compact emphatic launch
findings.claim: The combined lam and qad give the clause oath-response emphasis before kana names what is present.
findings.mechanism: Lam carries the force, qad reinforces certification, and the following kana supplies the proposition.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening sounds asserted rather than merely sequential.
findings.containment: This describes the local launch without claiming a separate oath word.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Detailing is added as a second function
findings.claim: Wa adds tafsil after tasdiq as a distinct member of the positive predicate list.
findings.mechanism: The coordinator is the carrier; tasdiq is the prior function and tafsil the new predicate.
findings.reader_payoff: The list accumulates functions instead of renaming confirmation.
findings.containment: Coordination does not establish the total number of possible functions.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Two functions remain distinct
findings.claim: Coordination lets revelation both confirm and detail without collapsing the actions into one label.
findings.mechanism: Wa links tasdiq to tafsil; their different verbal nouns supply the contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader distinguishes authentication from explanation.
findings.containment: The functions coexist and are not ranked.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Detailing has broad but bounded scope
findings.claim: Tafsil attaches to kulli shay, giving the detailing comprehensive scope within the verse's explanatory claim.
findings.mechanism: Tafsil is the carrier; kulli shay broadens its object, while the surrounding predicate list bounds the claim.
findings.reader_payoff: Comprehensiveness becomes intelligible as detailed exposition of a whole.
findings.containment: This is not an encyclopedia claim or a gloss of tafsil alone.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Detailing is an active operation
findings.claim: The Form II verbal noun tafsil presents separating and explaining as an operation performed by the discourse.
findings.mechanism: Tafsil is the carrier; its coordination after tasdiq places it among the discourse's actions.
findings.reader_payoff: Explanation appears as work that makes distinctions clear.
findings.containment: No claim is made that every possible object is exhaustively enumerated.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Totality belongs to the phrase
findings.claim: Kulli-shay gives the detailing distributive breadth while keeping the comprehensive claim attached to this predicate.
findings.mechanism: Kulli governs indefinite shay; tafsil is the independent predicate whose scope the construction expands.
findings.reader_payoff: The phrase is broad without making shay alone mean everything.
findings.containment: The scope is the verse's comprehensive formula, not an unbounded inventory.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: The construct builds totality
findings.claim: Kulli takes an indefinite genitive, and their construction together produces the sense of every thing.
findings.mechanism: Kulli carries totalizing scope; shay is the distinct complement that completes it.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader locates breadth in the phrase, not either noun alone.
findings.containment: The relation is local and does not settle the extent of every thing.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: A cadence opens into guidance
findings.claim: The terminal shay form closes the comprehensive phrase with a cadence immediately before the list turns to huda.
findings.mechanism: Shay carries the final hamza and tanwin; the following waw-huda sequence reopens movement toward guidance.
findings.reader_payoff: The sound boundary lets exposition resolve before direction begins.
findings.containment: This is a local sound-and-order effect, not a separate lexical sense.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: The noun is swept into totality
findings.claim: Shay receives its breadth from kulli and functions as the object inside a totality construction.
findings.mechanism: Shay is the carrier; kulli independently quantifies it, so the phrase supplies comprehensiveness.
findings.reader_payoff: The whole expression reads as comprehensive in form.
findings.containment: The construction, not shay alone, carries the totality.

epistemic.reason: The claim is anchored in the supplied focus wording and its distinct local relation.

findings.title: Guidance enters as a new list member
